messages:
support-ops: FYI — Acme reported a reproducible case where two parallel tool calls sometimes get their outputs assigned to the wrong tool_result. Customer: assistant calls `tool.search` and `tool.calc` in parallel; responses occasionally swap.

alex: Ugh. Do we have their request/response logs + correlation headers? Is this our router or downstream tool runner?

support-ops: They provided a few sample request payloads and the trace IDs. Example payload they sent (trimmed):
```json
{
  \"request_id\": \"acme-req-2026-03-12-77\",
  \"model\": \"gpt-open-1\",
  \"tools\": [
    {\"name\": \"search\", \"args\": {\"q\": \"pricing page\"}},
    {\"name\": \"calc\", \"args\": {\"expr\": \"sum([costs])\"}}
  ],
  \"parallel_tool_fanout\": true,
  \"meta\": {\"client_token\": \"tok-123\"}
}
```
They say the tool results arrive but the `tool_result.name` attached to the response doesn't always match the tool that produced the payload.

marie: Do they include any correlation token per tool call? We usually rely on `call_id` mapped to `tool_result` at the router layer. If the runner returns without `call_id` we try to correlate by order which is racy under parallel.

support-ops: Customer logs show `x-rw-call-id` on outgoing calls most of the time, but some returned responses from the runner miss that header. Sample paired responses (redacted):
```text
-> POST /runner/tool (out)  x-rw-call-id: call-77-search
<- 200 OK (in)  body: { \"result\": [...], \"call_id\": \"call-77-search\" }
-> POST /runner/tool (out)  x-rw-call-id: call-77-calc
<- 200 OK (in)  body: { \"result\": 42 }
```
Note: second incoming lacks `call_id` in body (runner didn't echo it). When that happens we sometimes map by the last-seen mapping and assign it to the wrong tool.

alex: That matches a race where we populate tool_result by matching on header first then fallback to FIFO. If runner strips the call_id or returns it in header only sometimes, and both responses land within the same scheduling quantum, we can flip.

eng-infra: Assigning to self — adding details. Our router keeps a transient correlation map keyed by `x-rw-call-id` and also by a monotonic `fanout_seq` per request. If runner responses don't contain either, we fall back to dequeuing by arrival order. The root cause looks like intermittent loss of `call_id` either in the runner or due to an intermediate proxy rewrite.

qa-tester: Repro steps I used locally (fast repro):
1) Enable `parallel_tool_fanout=true` on a test harness.
2) Instrument runner to randomly drop `call_id` on return (simulate bug).
3) Fire 10 concurrent requests with 2 tools each; observe mapping failures ~5-10% depending on timing.

qa-tester: Minimal repro script (node):
```js
// intentionally simplified
const axios = require('axios');
async function call() {
  await axios.post('https://api.redwood.internal/generate', {
    model: 'gpt-open-1',
    tools: [{name:'A'},{name:'B'}],
    parallel_tool_fanout: true
  }, {headers:{'x-client': 'qa'}})
}
for (let i=0;i<100;i++) call();
```
Run with a runner shim that drops `call_id` 10% of the time and you'll see swapped `tool_result.name` in the assembled generation.

marie: Immediate mitigation for customers: set `parallel_tool_fanout=false` or enable `force_echo_call_id=true` on the runner. Support can push config change.

support-ops: Acme asked for an ETA — can we give them a short-term workaround now and a long-term fix plan?

eng-infra: Short-term: push `parallel_tool_fanout=false` (serializes calls) or toggle runner to always echo `call_id` in both header+body. Long-term: robustify correlation by requiring signed correlation tokens and embedding per-tool sequence numbers (`tool_index`) in the model response assembly. We'll also log metric `tool_result_mismatch` when de-duped mapping happens.

alex: I can put up a patch to 1) require `call_id` in response parsing (drop and flag) and 2) add a fallback that checks `tool_result.signature` (hash of payload) + `tool_index` heuristics before assigning. But this needs runtime change and rollout plan.

sre-bot: @channel Incident created: INC-2026-1195 for \"tool_result association gaps\" :warning:

support-ops: I'll let Acme know the workaround and request logs/traces and permission to enable `force_echo_call_id` on their runner. Thanks team, will follow-up with logs once they grant access. :thumbsup:
